profile.name: sipak
profile.headline: Things I'm building.
profile.about: Small, sharp software, mostly close to the metal: a Forth in assembly, bare-metal firmware, terminal editors, and command-line tools that do one thing well. Each project is short enough to read in a sitting.

categories.title: Systems & Bare Metal
categories.blurb: No runtime, no libc, sometimes no operating system.

categories.title: Editors
categories.blurb: Modal text editors in the vi tradition, kept deliberately small.

categories.title: Web Apps
categories.blurb: Browser tools with no server and no build step.

categories.title: Educational Content
categories.blurb: I build courses to deepen my own expertise, because teaching a subject end to end is the best test of understanding it, and I share them freely with the community.

projects.title: NASMForth
projects.summary: A minimal Forth interpreter in a single x86-64 NASM source file for Linux. It uses raw syscalls instead of libc and builds to a ~9 KB binary.
projects.description: tiny barebones forth in NASM Assembler

projects.title: ESP32 Bare-Metal Firmware
projects.summary: A hands-on course in ESP32 firmware at the lowest level. It ends with a 208-byte Xtensa assembly image that the mask ROM boots directly, with no SDK, C or RTOS, plus a custom image packer verified against Espressif's tool.

projects.title: zen
projects.summary: ze is a small modal editor for the Linux terminal. It implements a minimal subset of vi and nothing more, so the whole program can be read in one sitting and owned by its user.
projects.description: a vi-ish editor, that gets out of the way.

projects.title: vibabel
projects.summary: A vi-style editor for writing pages of Borges' Library of Babel. Each page is located by its hexagon, wall, shelf, book and page, and saved under a page ID derived from that address.
projects.description: tiny vi + borges, what could be better?

projects.title: parc
projects.summary: parc (public archiver) encrypts files and their names with your SSH key. You can keep them in a public git repo, bucket or web server without revealing what they contain or what they're called.
projects.description: a simple cli to encrypt and store files publicly

projects.title: MemSRS
projects.summary: Terminal flashcards with spaced repetition. It reads plain CSV decks, schedules cards with an Anki-style ease/interval algorithm, and saves progress to SQLite after every card.
projects.description: A functional SRS command line app. Think Anki in your terminal.

projects.title: Web Reader
projects.summary: A private EPUB reader that runs entirely in your browser. Open a book from your device or a link, and it remembers your place. Nothing is uploaded, and a ?source= link opens a book directly.
projects.description: a fully in browser ereader app. saves state to your browser so you dont lose your progress. Bring your own epubs.

projects.title: Courseware
projects.summary: My learn-* courses, collected and readable as books. Each one is written to master a subject properly, from C, assembly and Zig to Go, React and philosophy, and is published openly so anyone can learn alongside me.
projects.description: An interactive library of the courses i've built for myself. Enjoy :-)
